defects.what: Dialog closes when a press starts inside the dialog and is released on the backdrop (for example while selecting text), because the click lands on the common ancestor, which is the backdrop.
defects.evidence: src/Dialog.tsx:109-111 (onClick on the backdrop checks only event.target === currentTarget). Probe: user.pointer([{keys:'[MouseLeft>]', target: button inside dialog}, {keys:'[/MouseLeft]', target: backdrop}]) printed 'drag-out closes? true'.

defects.what: The focus trap only knows about DOM descendants of the dialog. Pressing Tab from an element that a child has portaled out of the dialog (a popover, for example) jumps back to the first element instead of moving to the next one.
defects.evidence: src/Dialog.tsx:30-35 and 86-97 (items.indexOf(activeElement) is -1, so focus goes to items[0]). Probe: focus a createPortal'd button rendered inside the Dialog, press Tab, and it printed 'after tab from portaled: first'.

defects.what: The 'No results' message is a plain div outside the listbox with no role=status or aria-live, so screen readers are not told when the list is empty. aria-expanded stays true over an empty listbox.
defects.evidence: src/Combobox.tsx:138. Probe printed 'no results role/live: null null expanded true'.

defects.what: If the opener has been removed when the Dialog closes, focus falls to document.body and there is no fallback (such as an onCloseAutoFocus or a returnFocus target).
defects.evidence: src/Dialog.tsx:62-65. Probe that unmounts the trigger while the dialog is open printed 'trigger gone focus: BODY'.

defects.what: Background content is not made inert or aria-hidden, and there is no scroll lock. Modality relies only on aria-modal and the keydown Tab trap, so focus moved programmatically or by a pointer to the rest of the page is not trapped.
defects.evidence: src/Dialog.tsx has no inert, aria-hidden or focusin handling. Probe: main.closest('[aria-hidden],[inert]') returned null while the dialog was open.

defects.what: Tabs works out which tabs are enabled by reading the DOM after layout (JSON.stringify diffing plus a MutationObserver). This is clever but heavy. On the first render, before measurement, every enabled tab is briefly a tab stop, and nothing works under SSR until hydration.
defects.evidence: src/Tabs.tsx:47-60, 84-98.

defects.what: Combobox has no way to open the list from the pointer (no toggle button, and clicking the input does not open it), and Alt+ArrowDown/Up, Home and End are not handled. These are beyond the spec but are part of the full APG pattern.
defects.evidence: src/Combobox.tsx:64-95. Clicking the input leaves aria-expanded=false until a key is pressed.

strengths: All spec behaviour I probed passes. Tabs wrap past disabled tabs at both ends, Home/End work, selection follows focus, there is a single roving tab stop, and Tab/Shift+Tab move between the tablist and the panel. The Dialog is named and described, and its trap works with zero or one focusable child. Escape and backdrop close it and focus returns. The Combobox filters case-insensitively, aria-activedescendant always points at an element that exists, all-disabled lists and empty lists are handled, and clearing the text calls onChange(null).

Handles hard cases well. Nested dialogs use a layer stack so only the top one handles Escape and Tab. Escape in an open Combobox does not close the enclosing Dialog. The active option is tracked by value, so it survives option changes while open. Tabs re-measure when a child component adds or disables tabs.
The tests are thorough and behaviour-focused: 79 tests including 'hostile' edge cases, nested dialogs, and the README/exports checks. pnpm test and pnpm typecheck both pass cleanly.
Types are clean. They extend native HTML attributes with Omit for the props that conflict, every prop type is exported, and aria-label on TabList is required at the type level.
The README has prop tables and keyboard tables for every component and documents subtle rules, such as how clearing the text and committing in controlled mode behave.
reports.summary: Build A is a strong, careful implementation. All three components meet the WAI-ARIA requirements in the spec, including edge cases (disabled tabs at both ends, wrapping, zero or one focusable child, nested dialogs, options changing while open, every option disabled). The 79 meaningful tests pass and the typecheck is clean. I found no blockers or majors. The gaps are minor: dragging from inside the dialog to the backdrop closes it, the focus trap does not know about portaled descendants, 'No results' has no live region, the background is not inert and has no scroll lock, focus falls to body when the trigger is gone, and Tabs uses fairly heavy DOM measurement. The README is complete and well organised. Overall this is solid small-library quality.

defects.what: Dialog loses focus return when a child uses autoFocus. The opener is read from document.activeElement inside a passive useEffect, which runs after React has already focused the autoFocus element, so the 'opener' it saves is the element inside the dialog. On close that element is gone, so focus falls to <body>. The effect also overrides autoFocus by focusing the first tabbable.
defects.evidence: src/Dialog.tsx:25-33 (useEffect captures document.activeElement after commit). Probe: <button onClick=open>open</button><Dialog ...><button>a</button><input autoFocus/></Dialog>; click open -> activeElement BUTTON 'a' (autoFocus ignored); press Escape -> activeElement BODY (expected the 'open' button).

defects.what: Focus return has no fallback when the trigger has been removed. Focus goes to <body> instead of a sensible element.

judges.verdict: All 13 builds pass `pnpm test` and `pnpm typecheck`, and all meet the basic Tabs and Combobox keyboard spec, so what separates them is how robust the Dialog is. F, A and K have the most robust Dialogs: nested dialogs, autoFocus children and portaled children all work. C, E, G, H and I use a focusin trap that takes focus back from portaled children. That is a real composition limit, but it is a design trade-off, not a spec failure. B, D, J, L and M read the opener in a passive effect, so an autoFocus child is overridden and focus falls to body on close; the inspectors missed this for D, J, L and M. L and M also break with nested dialogs, and M cannot clear a selection back to null.

judges.verdict: All 13 builds pass pnpm test and typecheck, and all of them pass the basic spec probes for Tabs, Combobox and single-dialog behaviour. What separates them is how the Dialog holds up in harder cases. A, F and K handled every hard case I tried: autoFocus children, nested dialogs and portaled descendants.
